Evidence: logMemoryUpdate() opens the ambient getDb() insert; CRUD paths never thread workspace opts/ALS into it (createMemoryNote calls logMemoryUpdate without opts at agent-memory-store.ts:374-380; archive/suppress/update same at :596-603,:649-656,:704-711). dbScopeKey only discriminates cache keys; the audit insert goes to the process-global pool handle when called outside runWithDb.
Reproduction: Workspace-scoped createMemoryNote(..., {workspaceId}) writes the note to the workspace DB, then logMemoryUpdate inserts into the global/env DB (or throws swallowed) — memory_update_log rows land in the wrong database or are silently lost.
Root cause: Audit writer resolves its DB independently of the note's DB.
Impact: Audit trail for workspace memories is incomplete/misplaced; forensics and any future reader of memory_update_log are unreliable. Violates one-owner table contract in spirit.
Proposed fix: Thread the resolved db (or opts) into logMemoryUpdate: change signature to logMemoryUpdate(entry, db?) and pass the handle used for the note write; keep fire-and-forget semantics.
Required tests: Unit: create/archive/suppress in a fake two-DB setup assert log row lands in the same store as the note (extend memory-test-db harness).

Evidence: retrieveLocalCandidates filters lifecycleStatus === 'active' and discarded, but never calls isSuppressionActive() — unlike the PG path which filters at :73.
Reproduction: PG down (or workspace local-only) + a note with suppressUntil in the future (e.g. after discard soft-suppress) -> local retrieval returns the note in candidates/previews.
Root cause: Degraded retrieval lane omits the suppression predicate.
Impact: Soft-suppressed/discarded notes resurface in prompts during degraded mode; contradicts MEM-1a invariant (retrieval excludes actively-suppressed).
Proposed fix: Add .filter((r) => !isSuppressionActive(r)) to retrieveLocalCandidates (and consider the same in listLocal for includeSuppressed semantics).
Required tests: Unit: seed local mirror note with future suppressUntil; retrieval with db=null excludes it.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (ledger-recon): memory-retrieval.ts:168 suppressed filter in degraded mode

Evidence: readLocalMemoryNotes(agentId) with no workspaceId uses searchableWorkspaceScopes() and merges rows from every registered workspace folder into one map keyed only by note id.
Reproduction: Local-only/degraded read for agent X returns notes mirrored under workspace B when the same agentId exists in multiple workspaces.
Root cause: Unscoped local read is a cross-workspace union; callers (patchLocalNote :405, readLocal :421, listLocal :462, retrieveLocal :164) never pass scope.
Impact: Cross-workspace data bleed in degraded mode: an agent in workspace A can see workspace B's note content. Isolation violation (§30 / AGENTS tenant posture).
Proposed fix: Pass the resolved workspace scope into every local read (callers hold opts.workspaceId); keep multi-scope merge only for explicitly global admin reads.
Required tests: Unit: two scopes with same agentId different notes; scoped read returns only own scope; unscoped documented behavior pinned.

Evidence: logMemoryUpdate is exported flat (:51) but omitted from the memoriesGate object (:79-111), unlike every other lifecycle port.
Reproduction: Any consumer importing { memoriesGate } cannot reach logMemoryUpdate; callers must know the second import path.
Root cause: Facade assembly drift.
Impact: Contract shape and docs (Ports list marks it 'standalone export') disagree with the gate-object convention; future gating/codemods miss it.
Proposed fix: Either add logMemoryUpdate to memoriesGate or document the exclusion in the gate header; prefer adding (additive).
Required tests: Contract test: every flat function export exists on memoriesGate or is documented-exempt.

Evidence: generateNoteId(_agentId?) ignores the argument and returns buildNoteId() — underscore prefix documents it, but the port is exported with a misleading signature.
Reproduction: Call generateNoteId('agent-A') and generateNoteId('agent-B') -> ids carry no agent namespace.
Root cause: Legacy Continuum id format kept; per-agent sequences never implemented.
Impact: Callers reasonably assume per-agent id scoping; ids are globally day-scoped instead (fine today, misleading contract).
Proposed fix: Drop the parameter (breaking type change, low blast radius) or document explicitly in gate/types; docs standard already flags it.
Required tests: Type-level: generateNoteId() arity; docs Ports row updated.

Evidence: UpdateMemoryNotePatch.reason is required (no ?), but runtime does patch.reason ?? 'update'.
Reproduction: Call updateMemoryNote(agentId,id,{importanceScore:0.5} as any) -> succeeds with reason 'update'.
Root cause: Type/runtime disagreement on requiredness.
Impact: TS callers cannot omit reason without a cast, yet JS/dynamic callers can; audit reasons may be defaulted silently.
Proposed fix: Make reason optional (reason?: string) or enforce at runtime; align docs.
Required tests: Type-level + unit: omitted reason behavior pinned.

Evidence: Semantic lane: dynamic import + embedText inside try{...}catch{} with empty catch; weight env read raw with Math.min/max but NaN guard only after; failures are silent.
Reproduction: EMBEDDING_ENABLED=true + provider key present but endpoint hangs: embedText falls back to mock internally (ok). If embedText itself throws (e.g. profile lookup throw path), the catch{} swallows with zero telemetry.
Root cause: Empty catch around the semantic lane.
Impact: Silent degradation from hybrid to heuristic scoring; operators cannot see lane failures. Docs standard forbids silent console-only swallow; here it is not even console.
Proposed fix: Add logMetric on semantic-lane failure; consider hoisting the dynamic import.
Required tests: Unit: force embedText rejection -> retrieval still returns heuristics and emits metric.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-memories-narrow): memory-retrieval.ts:182-188 logMetric on semantic-lane failure; test memories.test.ts MEM-007

Evidence: searchByEmbedding builds raw SQL with COALESCE(embedding_vec::text, embedding) <=> $2::vector; failure caught by bare catch{} then JS fallback over 60 notes. The pgvector branch maps rank-based approximate scores (1 - idx*0.05) instead of real cosine.
Reproduction: With embedding_vec column present, returned scores are rank approximations, not similarity; with it absent, JS fallback returns real cosine — two different scoring semantics per environment.
Root cause: Raw-SQL path never aligned with JS scoring semantics.
Impact: Score values are not comparable across environments; callers ranking on score get environment-dependent ordering. No production caller today (Low usage risk).
Proposed fix: Either return real cosine in the SQL branch (compute from fetched vectors) or document rank-approx; add metric on fallback.
Required tests: Unit: both branches return monotone real-cosine scores on a fixed corpus.

Evidence: resolveAgentId caches misses and does a full findMany() scan of agents on every uncached alias miss; cache key includes dbScopeKey + workspaceId so per-tenant correct, but the scan is unbounded.
Reproduction: Point any tool call at a nonexistent agent name -> SELECT * FROM agents (all rows) per miss per process.
Root cause: Name-flex matching implemented as client-side scan instead of indexed query.
Impact: Cost scales with agent-table size on every unknown alias; hot-path risk if callers pass free text.
Proposed fix: Bound the scan (limit + lower(name) index) or query WHERE lower(name)=lower($1) OR id=$1.
Required tests: Perf: seed 10k agents, assert single indexed query plan / bounded rows.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-memories-narrow): agent-memory-store.ts:238-260 bounded ilike findFirst (no full-table scan); test memories.test.ts MEM-009

Evidence: listMemoryPreviews passes filter.limit ?? 50 straight into findMany with no upper clamp.
Reproduction: listMemoryPreviews(agent, {limit: 1e6}) -> unbounded result set materialized.
Root cause: No clamp convention in this domain (Messages caps at 200).
Impact: Unbounded preview fetches can exhaust memory/context; no caller currently passes large limits (Low exposure).
Proposed fix: Clamp to a MAX_PREVIEW_LIMIT (e.g. 200) with docs + type note.
Required tests: Unit: limit 10k clamps to MAX.

Evidence: embeddingsGate object exported from a non-gate file, not re-exported by memories-gate.ts; no importer found (grep).
Reproduction: Import embeddingsGate anywhere -> second public surface bypassing the domain facade.
Root cause: Leftover from SCL-2 port.
Impact: Two competing public contracts for the same domain; check-gates does not flag intra-domain duplication.
Proposed fix: Delete embeddingsGate or re-export it from memories-gate; keep one contract.
Required tests: Import-boundary check: only memories-gate.ts exports domain publics.

Evidence: Catch block: if isConnectionError -> local write and return; if attempt===2 -> throw; otherwise loop silently swallows the error and retries. A non-connection error on attempt 0/1 (e.g. invalid enum value) is retried twice pointlessly and only surfaces on the 3rd attempt. Final UPDATE_FAILED return is unreachable.
Reproduction: Force a deterministic non-connection insert error -> three attempts, throw on third; UPDATE_FAILED path never returns.
Root cause: Retry loop conflates id-collision retries with general error retries; dead return left behind.
Impact: Latency amplification (3x) for deterministic failures; misleading dead-code contract (docs flag it).
Proposed fix: Only retry on unique-violation/id-collision errors; rethrow others immediately; delete dead return or make it reachable.
Required tests: Unit: deterministic error -> exactly one insert attempt; collision (unique_violation) -> retried.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-memories-narrow): agent-memory-store.ts:396-408 collision-only retry, UPDATE_FAILED reachable; tests memories.test.ts MEM-012

Evidence: enforceCapsAllAgents loads every active note row (columns agentId only) to enumerate agents, then per-agent count+victim queries in chunks of 5.
Reproduction: Large vault (100k active notes) -> one full scan + 2 queries per agent per sweep tick (10min).
Root cause: No distinct-agent query; reuses findMany.
Impact: Sweep cost grows with total notes across all agents; DB pressure every 10 minutes in bullmq/inline sweeps.
Proposed fix: Use SELECT DISTINCT agent_id (index-only scan on agent_lifecycle_idx) and/or cap agents per tick.
Required tests: Perf: assert single DISTINCT query + chunked enforcement; measure sweep query count.

Evidence: Every PG write mirrors the full note row to a JSONL file via read-parse-rewrite under a lock; write failures are console-only (create) or swallowed .catch(()=>{}) (update/archive/suppress). No metric.
Reproduction: Make the mirror directory read-only -> PG write succeeds, mirror silently diverges; degraded reads later serve stale data.
Root cause: Best-effort mirroring without observability or reconciliation.
Impact: Local mirror can silently drift from PG; degraded mode then serves stale/wrong notes. Docs standard forbids silent swallow.
Proposed fix: Emit a metric/log on mirror failure uniformly; document mirror as best-effort replica with no convergence.
Required tests: Unit: mirror failure emits telemetry and does not fail the write.

Evidence: resolveEmbeddingProfile returns the FIRST embedding_model_profiles row (findFirst, no filter/order).
Reproduction: Insert two profiles -> resolution depends on row order, not on an active/default flag.
Root cause: Schema has no isDefault/active column; consumer picks first row.
Impact: Embedding model selection is nondeterministic across environments/insert order.
Proposed fix: Order by createdAt or add a default flag; document selection rule.
Required tests: Unit: two profiles -> documented deterministic pick.

Evidence: readMemoryNote access bump is read-modify-write (accessCount: note.accessCount + 1) without returning; concurrent reads lose increments.
Reproduction: Two concurrent readMemoryNote calls -> one increment lost.
Root cause: Non-atomic counter update.
Impact: accessCount/lastAccessed undercount under concurrency; low functional impact (telemetry-ish field).
Proposed fix: Use sql increment (accessCount = access_count + 1) single UPDATE.
Required tests: Unit: two sequential reads increment to 2 (existing); concurrency test optional.

Evidence: startMemorySweeper once-guard is module-global (started=true) and the timer sweeps every workspace DB; in-process inline mode + a colocated bullmq worker both running would double-sweep (sweep is idempotent per run, but audit rows double and cap races).
Reproduction: Run API process (inline) and worker process (bullmq) against same DBs -> each sweep tick runs twice (once per process) — idempotency limits damage; audit gets duplicate suppress_expire rows only if both observe the same expired row (update-then-find ordering makes that unlikely but unverified).
Root cause: No cross-process sweep lock.
Impact: Duplicate sweep work and potential duplicate audit rows; cost doubling.
Proposed fix: Advisory lock or worker-owns-sweep contract (already partly documented in heartbeat); add explicit lock if audit duplication observed.
Required tests: Low-confidence: requires multi-process repro; no test proposed now.

Evidence: Gate mixes value ports, object instances (sessionDiscards/reflectionThrottle), helpers (jaccardSimilarity), and aliases (runMemorySweep/discardFromContext) in one flat object; two naming layers for the same function.
Reproduction: n/a — structural.
Root cause: Facade grew by accretion.
Impact: Contract surface is wide (28 ports + 17 types); consumers can depend on internals (throttle instance, discards map) that are implementation state.
Proposed fix: Consider narrowing: expose behavior ports; keep instances only if tests/tools truly need mutation access (memories.test.ts uses them). Additive docs first.
Required tests: n/a (documentation-level).

Evidence: Retrieval discards are read via listDiscarded(input.agentId, input.channelId) BEFORE agent resolution; if callers pass an alias ('raven') while discard() was recorded with a UUID (or vice versa), discard filtering misses.
Reproduction: discardFromContext records key with resolvedAgentId (memory-lifecycle.ts:290-304 receives resolved id from tool path ctx.agentId — a UUID), retrieval receives input.agentId from middleware = agent.id (UUID) — consistent today; alias callers would drift.
Root cause: Key-space consistency depends on all callers passing the same id form; retrieval does not resolve.
Impact: Discarded notes may reappear when caller id forms differ (latent; current callers consistent).
Proposed fix: Normalize ids (resolveAgentId) before session-discard keying, or document UUID-only requirement.
Required tests: Unit: discard with alias then retrieve with alias (after resolution) hides note.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-memories-narrow): memory-retrieval.ts:53-72 + memory-lifecycle.ts:301-318 resolved-UUID key-space for session discards; tests memories.test.ts MEM-019

Evidence: Degraded archive/suppress use patchLocalNote which merges arbitrary patch keys into the JSONL row without validating lifecycle enum; and archiveMemoryNote degraded path never checks lifecycleStatus first.
Reproduction: Call archive on an already-suppressed local note -> patch sets lifecycleStatus archived, suppressUntil remains (inconsistent row).
Root cause: Local patch path is untyped merge.
Impact: Local mirror can hold impossible lifecycle combos; degraded reads may behave oddly (suppressed+archived).
Proposed fix: Constrain patchLocalNote keys to the same editable/lifecycle sets as PG paths.
Required tests: Unit: archive after suppress in degraded mode yields coherent row per contract.
